accuracy.evidence: Every probability is an exact binomial sum computed in pval_art.js and re-checked in Python with math.comb: B(30, 1/6) gives P(X = 9) = 3.09%, P(X ≥ 9) = 5.06%, P(X ≤ 9) = 98.03%, P(X ≥ 8) = 11.37%, P(X ≥ 10) = 1.97%, P(X ≥ 12) = 0.20%, P(X ≥ 6) = 38.36%; B(25, 0.2) gives P(X ≤ 1) = 2.74%, P(X = 1) = 2.36%, P(X ≥ 1) = 99.62%; B(10, 0.5) gives P(X ≥ 8) = 56/1024 = 5.47% and P(X = 8) = 4.39%. The definition and the reject-if-p ≤ α rule match the DfE A level content and exam-board mark schemes; the misreadings match the ASA 2016 statement.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors: P(X = x) used instead of the tail (9 sixes: 3.09% would wrongly reject, 5.06% does not), wrong tail for a lower-tail H₁, p read as P(H₀ true) or 1 − p as P(H₁ true), 'do not reject' read as proof of H₀, a small p read as a big effect, and rounding 5.06% down to 'about 5%' at the boundary.

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanics are about p itself: shading 'at least as extreme' with a side toggle and a draggable edge for an upper-tail die and a lower-tail machine, live p against α decisions, a true/false sort of readings of p = 0.03, a seeded simulation of 1000 runs under H₀ whose share converges on 5.06%, and sliding X to watch p cross 5% at the critical value. The shingle check passes against flag_tails.js and every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the definition by shading: a wrong edge says 'at least as extreme includes the observed 10 itself', the readout contrasts P(X ≥ x) with P(X = x), the X = 9 decision exposes the boundary case, the simulation shows p as a long-run share before the text names it, and the slider links p ≤ α to the critical region found in the earlier lesson.

predictions.evidence: Prediction 1 tempts P(X = 9), which the shading and readout disprove. Prediction 2 tempts 'Yes, 3% chance H₀ is true', which the sort rejects with the reason that p assumes H₀. Prediction 3 offers 'About 31, as P(X = 9) = 3.09%' and 'About 500'; the simulation lands near 51 in 1000.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with tagged wrong options: exact value instead of tail, wrong tail, too close to α (5.06% vs 5%), not rejecting read as proof, p read as the probability of H₀ or H₁, and p read as effect size. Each message names the slip and the fix.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 1.3 with notation kept to P(X ≥ 9) and one worked die example; adult text FK 8.3 (family limits 5.0/10.0). Sentences are short, and the definition is given once in words before any symbols.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: what p asks, extreme in the direction of H₁ with the worked value, the decision rule with the boundary case, what p does not mean. Adult paragraphs: standards, one- and two-tailed definitions and the link to critical regions, named mistakes, the lab. Content gate: no filler, under 12% overlap with 883, 952 and 995.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px canvas screenshots in light and dark: bar labels every 2 on phones, shaded tail bars also get an orange strip on the axis so tiny tails stay visible, side and decision tiles are 44 px tall, the true/false boxes give placed statements up to 66 px rows, and the readout line stays one or two lines.

accessibility.evidence: Button routes for every move: Side X ≥ / X ≤, Edge ◀ ▶ and Check; Reject / Do not reject; Pick then True or False; Run 200 more / Start again; Smaller X / Bigger X. Every action updates the canvas aria-label and live region, including the p readout and the challenge. walk.cjs ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations.
